description: Single registry of every dependency, static-analysis and scanner gate in CI, the severity each one blocks at, and every exclusion from those gates. scripts/check-security-gates.mjs fails the build when CI and this file disagree. A gate whose step runs a chain rather than the tool directly names the chain step and says so in its tool field; what this registry guarantees is that the named step exists in the blocking workflow and is not continue-on-error, which holds either way. A gate defaults to the workflow field below and may override it: the container, IaC and DAST scanners need Docker and a booted application, so they run in their own workflow rather than on every pull request.

gates.step: Semgrep gate (unaccepted findings block the merge)
IaC scan gate (unaccepted findings block the merge)
Signaling server image gate (unaccepted findings block the merge)
Web image gate (unaccepted findings block the merge)
DAST gate (unaccepted alerts block the merge)

exclusions.reason: The lock files it compares live in ~/.claude on a developer machine, so in CI the step has nothing to read and its exit code carries no signal.
Unmaintained, unsound, and yanked warnings on transitive crates with no upstream replacement. RUSTSEC vulnerabilities are still blocking in the step above.
The Windows test binary fails to load with STATUS_ENTRYPOINT_NOT_FOUND from a cross-CRT DLL mismatch; Windows cargo check and clippy stay strict and the full test suite runs on Linux.
Triaged Semgrep findings accepted as supply-chain hardening debt. Every entry carries a rule, reason, owner, and expiry that scripts/check-semgrep-findings.mjs enforces.
Reviewed non-credential fixtures keyed on (path, format); an entry that stops matching fails the scan as stale.
Triaged Trivy and ZAP findings. Every entry carries an id, a scanner, a reason, an owner and an expiry that scripts/check-scan-findings.mjs enforces, and an entry that matches nothing fails as stale.

RUSTSEC-2026-0258 (h2 unbounded empty DATA frames), Low severity, no fix published on the 0.3 line. h2 0.4 is already at the patched 0.4.16; h2 0.3.27 reaches the graph only through hyper 0.14, pinned by async-stripe 0.31 and oauth2 4.4, both of which use it as an HTTP client against Stripe and the identity provider. Clearing it needs the async-stripe 1.0 billing port and the oauth2 5.x call-site port. Re-check when async-stripe 1.0 ships stable.
